current.text: The latest Pelicans preview projects him well below last season, when he finished 108th in category leagues.
Some people expect him to start for the Pelicans and maybe close games in lineups with Zion Williamson at center.
Josh thinks there is way too much hype around him and sees him as possibly only the seventh or eighth man on the Pelicans. He called taking him at pick 119 a bad pick.
He went for 1 USD in an expert auction mock draft.
The Pelicans roster is crowded, with about eight players who could start, including him. It is unclear how the 240 minutes will be split.

Recent projected starting lineups do not include him. Dejounte Murray, Trey Murphy and Zion Williamson are seen as locked in, with Yves Missi likely at center and Jeremiah Fears or Herb Jones in the last spot.
Jamahl Mosley is the new head coach and brings a defense-first identity.
The Pelicans have a league-high 16 back-to-backs.
With a season end of March 28, the Pelicans play 4, 4 and 3 games in the fantasy playoff weeks, which the expert calls good.
Experts see the Pelicans as a weak team near the bottom of the West. One projects about 34 wins and no playoffs.

durable.text: The expert does not like his archetype. He needs more usage than a good team would give him and does little else.
He has a torn ACL in his injury history and finished strongly after coming back from it.
He blocks almost no shots for a forward, so a punt BLK team loses little with him. His FT% and low turnovers are mild positives.

note: Both sites price him at about 1 USD or less (Yahoo rank 150, ESPN 133), and 144 players get drafted, so he sits right at the edge of our player pool. The experts think the hype is too much and that he is a fragile bench piece on a crowded Pelicans roster. Let him go to waivers or take him only as a 1 USD final pick for a punt BLK build. Early in the season, check whether he starts or closes games next to Zion at center: last season's 17.7 points on 13.4 shots came with a bigger role than he is projected to get now.
